project.name: agmag
project.description: agm is a Rust CLI/TUI control panel for agent teams running on herdr/herdr-core: it meters tokens, context and subscription quota per agent, keeps a shared inbox and message log, enforces worker and budget policy, rotates agent sessions, and exposes BRANCHES.md writes and an MCP server for managers.

nodes.name: agy.rs
nodes.summary: Ingests recent Antigravity CLI (`agy`) sessions by scanning each conversation's `transcript.jsonl` under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain` (or `AGM_AGY_DIR`) and reading `conversation_summaries.db` read-only for workspace URIs used as the session cwd. It skips or de-duplicates `agm ask` sessions so the same conversation isn't counted twice, and returns aggregate ingest statistics into the agm store.

nodes.name: ingest_agy
nodes.summary: Runs the agy ingestion for a root and time window: loads conversation cwds from `conversation_summaries.db`, backfills `cwd` on existing agy sessions that lack it (excluding `agy://` ask paths), then for each discovered transcript skips sessions whose cwd equals the `agm ask` workdir or that already have an ask session with usage, otherwise calls `ingest_file`, sets the session identity from conversation id and cwd, de-duplicates a matching `agy://<conv_id>` ask session, and accumulates counts; per-file parse errors are logged to stderr and counted as skipped, while DB errors propagate as anyhow errors.

nodes.name: discover
nodes.summary: Scans `<root>/brain` for subdirectories containing `.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`, keeps only regular files whose modification time (milliseconds since UNIX epoch) is at or after `since_ms`, and returns the (conversation_id, log_path) pairs sorted by path, returning an empty vector if the brain directory cannot be read.

nodes.name: file_uri_to_path
nodes.summary: Converts a `file://` URI into a local path: strips the scheme and an optional `localhost` authority, percent-decodes the remainder, maps non-absolute paths to `\\server\share` on Windows or `//server/share` elsewhere, strips the leading slash before a Windows drive letter (e.g. `/C:/x`), and returns None when the prefix is missing or the decoded/trimmed path is empty, replacing `/` with `\` on Windows.

nodes.name: agy_quota.rs
nodes.summary: Reads the Antigravity CLI's plan quotas by running `agy --print /usage --output-format json`, converts agy's remaining-fraction buckets into used-percent quota snapshots for the agy-gemini, agy-3p and agy-argon providers, and stores them in the shared quota table via a background poller so the agm daemon loop never blocks.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a child process with timeout and process-tree kill for external CLI queries.

nodes.name: parse_usage
nodes.summary: Parses the trimmed stdout of agy /usage into a UsageParse, bailing if it is not valid JSON, if status is not "SUCCESS" (including the error message), or if command.data.groups is missing; it maps each bucket's id prefix to a provider and its "5h"/"weekly" window to minutes, converts remaining_fraction (validated finite and within 0..1) to a clamped used_percent with reset_time parsed from RFC3339, silently counts disabled buckets, counts unrecognized buckets as unknown, and groups the resulting QuotaWindows into per-provider QuotaSnapshots stamped with now_ms.

nodes.name: fetch_usage
nodes.summary: Runs the agy binary (overridable via AGM_AGY_BIN env var) with `--print /usage --output-format json --print-timeout 20s` in a temp workdir outside the repo, returning its stdout as a String even when it contains error JSON, and failing with the exit status plus up to 300 characters of stderr if stdout is empty or the command cannot be spawned.

nodes.name: AgyQuotaPoller
nodes.summary: Struct that polls agy /usage on its own interval: new() converts minutes to milliseconds (0 disables), and tick() non-blockingly collects the previous fetch's result from an mpsc channel, records its snapshots into the Store, warns once per distinct error message to stderr, and spawns a new thread running the injectable fetch closure when the interval has elapsed.

nodes.name: ask.rs
nodes.summary: This file implements the `agm ask` subcommand, which runs the agy (Gemini) CLI once in read-only/sandboxed plan mode and records its JSON output, token usage, and turn summaries into the agm store. It parses agy's JSON response, upserts a usage record with deduplication in a single transaction, and returns the answer text.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Parses agy's `--output-format json` output (status, response, conversation_id, model, usage), resolves or creates a session keyed by `agy://<conv>`, upserts a UsageRecord and deduplicates agy ask sessions inside one transaction when token metrics exist, inserts user (and on success assistant) TurnSummary rows, and bails with an error if agy's status is not SUCCESS — recording consumed tokens even in that failure case.

nodes.name: run_agy
nodes.summary: Runs the agy binary (overridable via AGM_AGY_BIN) once with `--mode plan --sandbox --output-format json` and a print timeout inside a temp working directory outside the repo, passing the question (and optional model) as arguments, then parses stdout as JSON and returns a contextual error including status, partial stdout, and stderr if the output is not valid JSON.

nodes.name: codex_quota.rs
nodes.summary: This module reads Codex account rate limits by driving `codex app-server` over JSON-RPC stdio (initialize then `account/rateLimits/read`), parses the used-percent windows, and stores them as quota snapshots for the agm CLI. It also provides a poller that schedules background fetches on an interval and warns once per distinct error, recording nothing on failures.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a child process with timeout and process-tree kill for external CLI queries.

nodes.name: parse_usage
nodes.summary: Parses a JSON-RPC response string, accepting a full envelope or bare result, reads the `primary` and `secondary` entries under `rateLimits`, and for windows with `usedPercent` in 0.0..=100.0, `windowDurationMins` of 300 or 10080, and a `resetsAt`, builds a single `QuotaSnapshot` for provider `codex` at `now_ms`, returning a UsageParse (with zero unknown/disabled) or bailing if no valid windows exist.

nodes.name: fetch_usage_inner
nodes.summary: Takes a spawned `codex app-server` child, its binary name, and a deadline; it reads stdout lines on a spawned thread, writes an `initialize` and then an `account/rateLimits/read` JSON-RPC request to stdin, waits for responses matching ids 1 and 2 before the deadline or bails on timeout/disconnect/error, and returns the `result` serialized as a JSON string.

nodes.name: CodexQuotaPoller
nodes.summary: A struct holding an interval, a boxed fetch closure, the last start time, a pending channel receiver, and the last error; its `tick` checks a completed background fetch and records usage into the Store, starts a new fetch thread when the interval elapses and none is pending, and its `warn` prints a stderr warning only when the error message changes.

nodes.name: correlate.rs
nodes.summary: Correlates live herdr-core terminals with log sessions in the agm CLI by matching app/source, normalized cwd, and time windows, writing automatic or rotation-based links into the store.

nodes.name: link_all
nodes.summary: Scans live terminals without an agm.parent_rotation label, finds candidate sessions by matching source, normalized cwd, and a start-time window (with OpenCode allowed to relink auto-linked terminals to a newer session), then links only one-to-one terminal/session pairs via Store::link_terminal with source "auto", returning the count of new links.

nodes.name: link_codex_rotation
nodes.summary: In a transaction, looks up a Codex successor session for a terminal by requiring a user turn from requested_ms whose summary starts with the [agm-rot:<rot_id>] tag, matching normalized cwd and no existing terminal link; if exactly one match exists it updates the terminal with link_source "rotation" and returns the session id, otherwise returns the existing linked session or None.

nodes.name: hook.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the `agm hook statusline` subcommand of the agm CLI: it ingests the JSON that Claude Code pipes to a statusLine command on stdin, records quota/context/terminal-link data into the store, and prints a short status string for display. It also provides the installer that adds agm's statusLine entry to Claude Code's settings.json without overwriting someone else's.

nodes.name: install_statusline
nodes.summary: Reads settings_path as JSON (treating a missing file as an empty object, but propagating other I/O errors and invalid-JSON errors), refuses with an error if it is not an object or if an existing statusLine is not agm's own (`hook statusline`), otherwise writes a pretty-printed statusLine command pointing at agm_exe and returns Added or AlreadyInstalled.

nodes.name: statusline
nodes.summary: Parses rate_limits five_hour/seven_day entries into QuotaWindows and inserts a Claude QuotaSnapshot, then for a non-empty transcript_path resolves the session via path_key, stores context_window_size and a computed used-token ContextSnapshot, upserts/links the hc_terminal as a live claude-code terminal when given, and finally returns a `model · ctx N% · 5h N% left · 7d N% left` string.

nodes.name: ingest.rs
nodes.summary: Implements incremental ingestion of Codex and Claude session JSONL logs into the agm CLI's SQLite store: it discovers recently modified log files, parses each line into events (meta, model, effort, usage, quota, context, turns), and persists them transactionally while tracking per-file read cursors and aggregate stats.

nodes.name: ingest_file
nodes.summary: Incrementally ingests one JSONL log file inside a single unchecked SQLite transaction: it opens the file, computes an FNV-1a hash of the first 4096 bytes to validate the saved cursor (resetting the session's stored data if the file shrank or its head changed), seeks to the saved offset, seeds the parser with the stored model and last timestamp when resuming, parses each complete newline-terminated line and writes resulting ParseEvents to the store via set_meta/set_model/set_effort/upsert_usage/insert_quota/set_context/insert_turn while counting unknown and bad lines, then records line stats, saves the new cursor (offset, size, mtime, head hash), commits, and returns per-file IngestStats or an anyhow error on I/O or store failures.

nodes.name: discover_source
nodes.summary: Recursively walks a root directory with walkdir and returns a sorted vector of .jsonl file paths whose modification time (in ms since the Unix epoch) is at least since_ms, additionally requiring a 'rollout-' filename prefix for Codex sources, plus a count of directory-walk errors excluding NotFound errors; it returns an empty list when the root does not exist.

nodes.name: ingest_all
nodes.summary: Runs ingest_source for both the Codex and Claude roots under the given Roots, accumulates their IngestStats into one total, and returns that combined result, propagating any error from either source.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: This file is the crate root of the agm CLI library; it contains no logic of its own and solely declares the public module tree (actions, git, config, store, daemon, mcp, etc.) that makes up the CLI's functionality. It acts as the entry point that wires all submodules together for the rest of the binary to use.

nodes.name: model.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the data model for the agm CLI: serde-derived enums and structs representing usage records, quota/context snapshots, session metadata, and parsed turn events, plus two helper functions for text summarization and timestamp parsing.

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Collapses all whitespace in the input text into single spaces and returns the result unchanged if it is at most 200 characters, otherwise truncates it to the first 199 characters and appends an ellipsis character.

nodes.name: parse_rfc3339_ms
nodes.summary: Parses a UTC timestamp string in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS(.fff)?Z form by checking its length, separators and digits, validating calendar ranges (including leap years), and returning milliseconds since the Unix epoch as Some(i64), or None for any malformed or out-of-range input.

nodes.name: opencode.rs
nodes.summary: Reads OpenCode v2 session data from the read-only SQLite database opencode.db, ingesting only session_v2 and session_message rows into the agm store. It tracks incremental progress with a dual cursor and converts OpenCode messages into session metadata, token usage, context snapshots, and turn summaries.

nodes.name: ingest_opencode
nodes.summary: Scans new OpenCode session_message rows from the given SQLite database into the Store, returning IngestStats; it skips missing databases, uses a (time_updated, rowid) cursor with optional full rescan on model-key version changes, upserts session metadata, assistant usage/context and turn summaries, user turn summaries, counts bad JSON rows, and commits cursor/settings updates in a transaction.

nodes.name: opencode_models.rs
nodes.summary: Read-only OpenCode model catalog that maps `providerID/id` keys to their context window sizes by parsing the output of `opencode api GET /api/model`, with a process-wide cache. It lets the agm daemon look up token context limits without hitting the network on every loop or trusting a possibly stale local models.json.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a child process with timeout and process-tree kill for external CLI queries.

nodes.name: ModelCatalog
nodes.summary: Struct wrapping a BTreeMap from `providerID/id` to a u64 context-window size, with from_json/from_value parsers that accept either a `{location,data:[...]}` envelope or a bare array and skip items missing providerID, id, or a non-zero `limit.context`; context() returns Option<u64> for a key (filtering zeros), cached() runs load() once via a OnceLock and clones the result (None on failure), load() tries the `opencode` then `opencode.cmd` binaries and returns the last error or `opencode not found`, and len()/is_empty() report the entry count.

nodes.name: load_with
nodes.summary: Spawns the given binary with args `api GET /api/model`, pipes stdout and discards stderr, reads the output on a separate thread through an mpsc channel with a 5-second LOAD_TIMEOUT deadline to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock, then polls child.try_wait until exit within the same deadline; on timeout, read error, or non-success exit status it kills the process tree via kill_tree and returns an error, otherwise it parses the collected text into a ModelCatalog via from_json.

nodes.name: opencode_quota.rs
nodes.summary: Polls the OpenCode Go plan quota by spawning `opencode api GET /api/experimental/usage/limits`, parsing the JSON into per-window usage snapshots (rolling/weekly/monthly) that are persisted via the Store, and exposing a non-blocking interval poller used by the agm CLI. Missing or malformed meters are counted as unknown rather than fabricated as 0% or 100%.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a child process with timeout and process-tree kill for external CLI queries.

nodes.name: parse_usage
nodes.summary: Parses the trimmed stdout as JSON (erroring on invalid JSON), returns an empty default UsageParse when data is null, counts one unknown when the go object is missing, and for each known meter (rolling=300, weekly=10080, monthly=43200 minutes) clamps percent to 0-100, converts resetsAt from ms to seconds, and records the limited flag, counting unrecognized keys or meters with missing/null fields as unknown and emitting a single opencode-go QuotaSnapshot only if at least one valid window exists.

nodes.name: fetch_with
nodes.summary: Spawns the given binary with arguments `api GET /api/experimental/usage/limits`, reads its piped stdout on a helper thread, and waits with recv_timeout until the shared deadline, killing the whole process tree (taskkill /T /F on Windows) and returning an error on timeout, read failure, or nonzero exit status, otherwise returning the captured stdout text.

nodes.name: OpenCodeQuotaPoller
nodes.summary: Stateful poller holding an interval in milliseconds, an injectable Arc fetch closure, and a pending channel receiver; its tick method returns immediately when the interval is non-positive, drains any finished background fetch and records it via record_usage (deduplicating repeated warnings to stderr), and when due spawns a thread running the fetch closure, while new converts a minutes interval to milliseconds with saturating arithmetic.

nodes.name: agy.rs
nodes.summary: This file implements the transcript.jsonl reader for the Antigravity CLI (agy) in the agm CLI: the AgyParser struct parses each JSONL line of conversation steps (USER_INPUT, PLANNER_RESPONSE, ignored/system kinds) and emits turn summaries, model changes, usage records with dedupe keys, and context snapshots.

nodes.name: AgyParser
nodes.summary: A LogParser implementation holding an optional seeded model and last-seen timestamp whose parse_line method deserializes a JSONL line, updates last_ts from created_at, and for USER_INPUT lines extracts and summarizes the user request into a User TurnSummary (failing with MissingTimestamp when no timestamp is available), for PLANNER_RESPONSE lines emits a Model event when the non-empty model field changes, computes Usage with input/cache-read/output/reasoning tokens (output being max of output_tokens and thinking_tokens, cache_write always 0) plus a ContextSnapshot when input+cache_read > 0, deduplicating usage by step_index or byte offset, and returns Unknown for unrecognized types, Ignored for known but empty kinds, or the collected events otherwise.

nodes.name: claude.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the LogParser used by the agm CLI to parse Claude Code JSONL log lines into a timeline of typed ParseEvents (session metadata, model/effort changes, token usage, context snapshots, and turn summaries). It is the parser selected for Source::Claude during log ingestion and keeps per-session state so metadata and model/effort transitions are emitted only when they change.

nodes.name: ClaudeParser
nodes.summary: Stateful LogParser that deserializes each Claude Code log line with serde_json (returning ParseError::BadJson on malformed input), emits a one-time ParseEvent::Meta from sessionId/cwd/version/timestamp once those fields appear, and on 'assistant' lines emits Model/Effort changes when the model or effort differs from stored state plus a Usage record (keyed by message id, reading input/cache/output/thinking counters) and Context snapshot of saturated input+cache tokens, while producing summarized Turn events for assistant and 'user' text/tool-use content and returning LineOutcome::Unknown or Ignored for unhandled kinds.

nodes.name: codex.rs
nodes.summary: Implements a LogParser for Codex JSONL session logs, converting line records into normalized agm parse events such as session metadata, model/effort changes, token usage, context/quota snapshots, and turn summaries. It tracks the current model state and ignores or marks unknown Codex record types.

nodes.name: CodexParser
nodes.summary: A default-initialized LogParser that stores an optional current model, seeds it via seed_model, and parses Codex JSON lines in parse_line by dispatching on record type to emit Meta, Model/Effort, Usage, Context/Quota, or Turn events; it ignores unsupported records, returns Unknown for unrecognized types, and handles missing/malformed fields with defaults or ignored outcomes.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the shared parsing contract for agm's line-based session log parsers, re-exporting the agy, claude, and codex submodules and providing a source-to-parser factory plus a ParseError type. It is the dispatch point that turns a detected Source into a mutable LogParser used to stream log lines into LineOutcome events.

nodes.name: parser_for
nodes.summary: Returns a boxed LogParser for the given Source by constructing the default CodexParser, ClaudeParser, or AgyParser, and panics via unreachable! for Source::OpenCode because that source is not read line by line.

nodes.name: LogParser
nodes.summary: A trait implemented by each source-specific parser, requiring parse_line to turn a single log line plus its byte offset into a LineOutcome or ParseError and seed_model to set the current model name, with an optional seed_last_ts hook that defaults to doing nothing.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the SQLite-backed persistence layer for the agm CLI: a Store wrapping a rusqlite Connection that opens or creates the database, sets WAL mode and a 5-second busy timeout, and migrates the schema up to version 4 inside a write transaction with busy/locked retries. It provides write and read operations for sessions, token usage, quota snapshots, conversation turns, context snapshots, and file-ingestion cursors, using savepoints for atomic multi-statement writes so the daemon and CLI can share the database safely.

nodes.name: Store
nodes.summary: A struct holding a single rusqlite Connection that exposes the database API for agm, with constructors open (creating parent directories and opening a file-backed DB) and open_in_memory, savepoint-wrapped writers for sessions/usage/turns/quota/cursors, and a conn() accessor returning the underlying connection.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: A private constructor that configures a Connection with a 5-second busy_timeout, enables WAL and foreign keys via retry_busy, returns early without a write lock if PRAGMA user_version is already at least 4, otherwise runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE and migrates from the stored version (applying schema.sql/schema_v2.sql, normalizing Windows session/cursor paths for v1 databases, adding rotation/terminal columns and schema_v3.sql for v3, and adding the sessions.effort column for v4), rolling back and returning the error on failure or committing and returning the Store on success.

nodes.name: upsert_usage
nodes.summary: Inserts a UsageRecord's token counters (input_uncached, cache_read, cache_write, output, reasoning, each converted from u64 to i64 with try_from, which errors on overflow) into the usage table for session sid, updating all fields on conflict of (session, dedupe_key), then refreshes the session's last_ms to the max timestamp across usage and turns, all inside a savepoint that is rolled back on error.

nodes.name: v2.rs
nodes.summary: This file implements the SQLite (rusqlite) data-access API for the agm CLI's v2 tables — terminals, inbox, messages, budgets, actions, and settings — by adding methods on Store and serializable row structs. It handles upserts, deduplicated inbox opening/resolving, and status tracking for managed terminals.

nodes.name: TerminalRow
nodes.summary: A serializable struct holding one terminal's record (address, name, app, cwd, labels, task/role, state, status, turn, parent, timestamps, exit code, session link, handoff state, managed flag, launch spec) with a Default impl that sets handoff_state to "active" and turn/created_ms to 0.

nodes.name: upsert_terminal
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a terminals row keyed by address with an ON CONFLICT upsert that coalesces new non-null fields over existing ones, keeps the max of reported/turn-like flags and the original created_ms, derives task/role from agm.task/agm.role labels when absent, and serializes labels to JSON (propagating serialization errors via ?).

nodes.name: resolve_inbox_many
nodes.summary: Marks many inbox ids resolved in one transaction using a named SAVEPOINT, returning early without doing anything if ids is empty, releasing the savepoint on success and rolling it back (preserving any existing reply, since it only sets resolved_ms) if any UPDATE fails.

nodes.name: open_inbox_keyed
nodes.summary: Opens an inbox item deduplicating by (terminal, source, kind): if no unresolved item with that key exists it inserts one and returns Some(new rowid), otherwise it updates the existing item's text in place and returns None.

nodes.name: actions.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the mutating agm actions: inbox send/reply/done-dismissal, successor spawn with prechecks and brief delivery, authorize, interrupt, managed-launch recording and cleanup of finished terminals, with caller identification.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typed error enums with exit codes (BriefUndelivered) and a trait-based Hc client for testability.

nodes.name: classify_caller
nodes.summary: Classifies a terminal identity into a Caller role.

nodes.name: detect_caller
nodes.summary: Detects the current caller from environment and herdr state.

nodes.name: parse_done_selectors
nodes.summary: Parses selector arguments for the done command into filters.

nodes.name: dismiss_done
nodes.summary: Dismisses processed inbox reports matching selectors/filters, returning a DoneReport of dismissed and skipped items.

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Sends a formatted message to a terminal via herdr and records it in the inbox store.

nodes.name: reply
nodes.summary: Replies to an inbox message by resolving its sender and sending back.

nodes.name: spawn_precheck
nodes.summary: Validates a spawn request (template, budget, caller authority) before launching.

nodes.name: spawn
nodes.summary: Spawns a new worker terminal from a template through the herdr client and registers it.

nodes.name: prepare_rotation_spawn
nodes.summary: Prepares a successor spawn for session rotation.

nodes.name: send_spawn_brief
nodes.summary: Delivers the template brief to a spawned terminal, failing with BriefUndelivered when delivery cannot be confirmed.

nodes.name: authorize
nodes.summary: Grants or checks authorization for a terminal action.

nodes.name: set_managed_launch
nodes.summary: Records a managed launch spec for a terminal so it can be rotated later.

nodes.name: interrupt
nodes.summary: Interrupts a running terminal agent.

nodes.name: eligible_cleanups
nodes.summary: Selects finished or idle terminals eligible for cleanup.

nodes.name: execute_cleanup_batch
nodes.summary: Closes eligible terminals in a batch and produces a CleanupReport.

nodes.name: Caller
nodes.summary: Identifies who is invoking an action (role and terminal).

nodes.name: BriefUndelivered
nodes.summary: Error type signalling the template brief was not delivered, mapped to exit code 3.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: Loads and models agm configuration: provider billing, model price tables with built-in defaults, context windows and worker/budget policy, plus cost and context-percent helpers.

nodes.name: model_id_candidates
nodes.summary: Generates candidate model ids for price/context lookup fallback.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads the agm config file, falling back to defaults.

nodes.name: context_window
nodes.summary: Resolves the context-window size for a model.

nodes.name: price_for
nodes.summary: Finds the price entry for a model with provider fallbacks.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Top-level configuration struct with pricing, models, providers and policy.

nodes.name: Policy
nodes.summary: Worker/budget policy settings with defaults.

nodes.name: daemon.rs
nodes.summary: Applies herdr event stream updates (snapshots, terminal and status events) into the store for the long-running agm daemon.

nodes.name: apply_event
nodes.summary: Dispatches a herdr event to snapshot, terminal or status handlers and updates the store.

nodes.name: apply_snapshot
nodes.summary: Applies a full terminal snapshot to the store.

nodes.name: apply_status
nodes.summary: Updates terminal agent status from a status event.

nodes.name: dashboard.rs
nodes.summary: hand-rolled ANSI/comfy-table TUI dashboard rendering terminals, budgets, inbox, system monitor and reports, with view/command parsing and styled-text helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Large rendering module built from hand-written ANSI escape sequences, styled text helpers and comfy-table, without a TUI framework.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Builds a Snapshot of terminals, budgets and stats from the store for rendering.

nodes.name: terminals_table
nodes.summary: Builds the terminals table widget.

nodes.name: wrap_styled_items
nodes.summary: Wraps styled items to a given width.

nodes.name: render_header
nodes.summary: Renders the dashboard header with summary info.

nodes.name: system_verdict
nodes.summary: Derives an overall system health verdict from sysmon stats.

nodes.name: machine_lines
nodes.summary: Renders CPU and memory machine lines.

nodes.name: agent_lines
nodes.summary: Renders per-agent resource usage lines.

nodes.name: render_footer
nodes.summary: Renders the footer with key hints and status.

nodes.name: render_view
nodes.summary: Renders the currently selected view.

nodes.name: render_section
nodes.summary: Renders an individual dashboard section (terminals, inbox, budgets, usage, etc.).

nodes.name: sanitize_one_line
nodes.summary: Sanitizes text into a single safe terminal line.

nodes.name: parse_done_tui
nodes.summary: Parses done command arguments typed in the TUI.

nodes.name: parse_command
nodes.summary: Parses a TUI command line into a TuiCmd.

nodes.name: Snapshot
nodes.summary: Aggregate view-model of terminals, budgets and system stats.

nodes.name: Section
nodes.summary: Enum of dashboard sections with name helpers.

nodes.name: TuiCmd
nodes.summary: Enum of commands accepted by the TUI command line.

nodes.name: load_template
nodes.summary: Loads an HcTemplate definition (command, brief) from disk.

nodes.name: call

nodes.name: run_args
nodes.summary: Builds argument vector for hc run.

nodes.name: Hc
nodes.summary: Trait abstracting herdr-core operations for testing.

nodes.name: HcCli
nodes.summary: Process-based implementation of Hc.

nodes.name: launch.rs
nodes.summary: Parses and rewrites terminal launch command lines into a LaunchSpec and builds successor argv for rotation, filtering codex and claude flags and checking the Claude hook is installed.

nodes.name: parse_cmd_tokens
nodes.summary: Tokenizes a command line string respecting quotes.

nodes.name: parse_launch_spec
nodes.summary: Derives a LaunchSpec from a raw launch command.

nodes.name: check_claude_hook_installed
nodes.summary: Checks Claude settings for the agm hook.

nodes.name: filter_codex
nodes.summary: Filters codex args for the successor launch.

nodes.name: filter_claude
nodes.summary: Filters claude args for the successor launch.

nodes.name: LaunchSpec
nodes.summary: Persistable launch specification with JSON conversion.

nodes.summary: Budget and context policy ticks: computes provider usage percent against budgets, blocks spawns over budget and notifies about context pressure.

nodes.name: provider_percent
nodes.summary: Computes provider quota/budget usage percent.

nodes.name: spawn_blocked_by_budget
nodes.summary: Decides whether a spawn is blocked by exceeded budget.

nodes.name: session_context_pct
nodes.summary: Computes a session context fill percentage.

nodes.summary: Sends a policy notification to the relevant terminal.

nodes.summary: Periodic check of budgets, notifying on thresholds.

nodes.name: harness_markdown.py
nodes.summary: Offline, dependency-free Markdown checker that parses documents into visible lines, heading anchors and links, and reports lint issues (whitespace, fences, heading levels, tables, link targets, anchors). Not a CommonMark parser; it is the shared base for the harness linter.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses frozen/ordered dataclasses for Issue and regex-driven line scanning with unicodedata-based GitHub-style slugging.

nodes.name: harness_routing.py
nodes.summary: Declares explicit routing contracts (model routing, NVIDIA background models, safety rules, skill routing) and verifies that the harness docs' marker-delimited contract tables match them. Also checks model IDs, retired slugs and leaked API credentials.
nodes.languageNotes: Contracts are enforced by comparing HTML-comment-delimited Markdown tables against module-level constant dicts.

nodes.name: lint_harness.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point of the harness linter: walks the repo for Markdown files, parses them, runs model-ID, link and contract checks, redacts secrets and prints a text or JSON report with a nonzero exit code on issues.

nodes.name: Issue
nodes.summary: Frozen, orderable dataclass describing one lint finding (path, line, code, message).

nodes.name: Document
nodes.summary: Mutable dataclass holding a parsed document's text, visible lines, anchors, links and accumulated issues, with an error() helper.

nodes.name: slug
nodes.summary: Builds a GitHub-style heading anchor slug by stripping links, HTML and code ticks, lowercasing and keeping letters, marks, numbers, hyphens and underscores.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Normalizes a reference-link label by collapsing whitespace and casefolding.

nodes.name: cells
nodes.summary: Splits a Markdown table row into cells on unescaped pipes.

nodes.name: visible_lines
nodes.summary: Scans the text line by line, tracking code fences, to collect visible lines and heading anchors while reporting whitespace, conflict markers, heading skips, unclosed fences, H1 count and final newline issues.

nodes.name: inline_links
nodes.summary: Extracts inline link destinations from a line with balanced-parenthesis scanning and reports unclosed or invalid destinations.

nodes.name: collect_links
nodes.summary: Gathers inline and reference-definition links from visible lines (ignoring inline code and comments) and flags duplicate definitions and undefined reference labels.

nodes.name: check_tables
nodes.summary: Validates Markdown tables: separator needs an adjacent header and every row must match the header's column count.

nodes.name: parse_document
nodes.summary: Builds a Document from path and text, checking BOM and NUL bytes then running visible-line, link and table passes.

nodes.name: check_links
nodes.summary: Validates collected links against the filesystem: rejects drive/absolute/unsafe paths, root escapes, missing files, wrong casing, and missing heading anchors in linked Markdown.

nodes.name: exact_case
nodes.summary: Checks that each path component matches a real directory entry with exact casing, for case-sensitive portability.

nodes.name: check_model_ids
nodes.summary: Scans a document line by line for credential-like secrets, retired model slugs, and DeepSeek/NVIDIA model IDs, validating them and their variants against the verified catalog (archived docs exempt).

nodes.name: contract
nodes.summary: Validates one marker-delimited contract table in a document against an expected key/value dict, reporting structural, duplicate, unexpected and missing-key policy errors.

nodes.name: check_contracts
nodes.summary: Applies every contract in CONTRACTS to its required docs file and returns issues for missing policy documents.

nodes.name: load_documents
nodes.summary: Walks the root directory, skipping ignored and symlinked folders, reads each Markdown file as UTF-8, parses it and records IO issues.

nodes.name: lint
nodes.summary: Runs the full lint pipeline over a root: loads documents, checks required files, model IDs, links and contracts, then redacts secrets and returns a sorted Report.

nodes.name: Report

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README introduces agm as a control panel beside herdr/herdr-core that meters tokens, context fill and subscription quota, surfaces an inbox of blocked agents, and lets you intervene with budgets, rotation and handoffs. It is a single Rust binary (v0.4.0) and the CHANGELOG tracks its evolution. Start here for the vocabulary the rest of the tour relies on.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: main.rs defines the clap command tree and dispatches each subcommand, while lib.rs declares every module of the crate so the binary and the integration tests share one library. ops.rs holds the command implementations behind the CLI, such as branch file access, the daemon loop and replay.
tour.languageLesson: Rust crates split into a thin binary (main.rs) and a library (lib.rs); integration tests in tests/ import the library as agmag::..., which is why most logic lives outside main.rs.

tour.title: Core Domain Model and Config
tour.description: model.rs is the most widely depended-upon file: Source, Usage, quota and context snapshots and parse events are shared by ingestion, storage, policy and reporting. config.rs loads providers and price tables, with built-in defaults shipped as TOML assets. Understanding these types makes every later layer easier to read.
tour.languageLesson: Rust enums such as Source model a closed set of agent kinds, and pattern matching forces every consumer to handle each variant.

tour.title: Log Parsers
tour.description: Each agent writes a different log format, so the parse module defines a LogParser trait and a parser_for factory with one implementation per source: Claude JSONL transcripts, Codex rollouts and Antigravity logs. They turn raw lines into the model events from the previous step, such as usage, context and quota.
tour.languageLesson: A trait plus a factory function gives runtime polymorphism: callers hold a boxed LogParser without knowing the concrete format.

tour.title: Ingestion Pipeline
tour.description: ingest.rs discovers log roots, tails files incrementally with cursors and feeds the parsers, so token and context numbers stay current without rereading whole transcripts. Separate modules handle OpenCode's SQLite database and Antigravity logs, and hook.rs installs the Claude statusline hook that supplies live context data.

tour.title: SQLite Store and Schema
tour.description: The Store wraps SQLite with schema initialization, busy-retry and savepoints, and is the second most depended-upon module. Versioned SQL schemas define sessions, usage, quota and cursors, then terminals, messages, inbox, budgets, actions and rotations, with v3 adding a time index for statistics.
tour.languageLesson: Schema migrations are additive and versioned (v1 to v3), so existing databases upgrade in place without losing metering history.

tour.title: Quota and System Metering
tour.description: Quota pollers query Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode for subscription windows and reset times, and sysmon.rs attributes CPU and memory load to agent processes. Their results land in the store tables you just saw and feed the dashboard and policy.

tour.title: Daemon and herdr Integration
tour.description: hc.rs wraps the herdr-core CLI, and daemon.rs applies the herdr event stream into the store, creating terminals and inbox items when agents block. correlate.rs links ingested sessions to terminals by cwd and app so usage is attributed to the right agent.

tour.title: Actions, Policy and Rotation
tour.description: actions.rs implements send, reply, spawn and kill with worker limits; policy.rs checks budgets and context fill; and rotation.rs runs a state machine that requests a handoff and spawns a successor session. launch.rs rewrites launch command lines for those successors. Together they implement the controlled intervention described in the README.
tour.languageLesson: State machines in Rust are naturally expressed as enums with match arms, making illegal transitions visible at compile time.

tour.title: BRANCHES.md Writer and MCP Server
tour.description: branches.rs validates and upserts entries in the BRANCHES.md registry under a lock, using git.rs for HEAD and clean-tree checks. mcp.rs exposes agm tools, including branch updates, over a stdio JSON-RPC server so agents can call agm directly.

tour.title: Reporting, TUI and Dashboard
tour.description: report.rs summarizes sessions and usage by window with local-time grouping, and dashboard.rs and tui.rs render those results plus budgets and the inbox with hand-written ANSI escapes and comfy-table. This is the operator-facing view of everything collected beneath it.

tour.title: Tests and Fixtures
tour.description: Integration tests share a fake herdr client from tests/common and exercise actions, policy, MCP, branches and the heavy rotation suites. Sanitized Claude and Codex JSONL fixtures give parsers and ingestion realistic input, and tools/sanitize_fixture.py produces them.

tour.title: Harness Docs and Lint Scripts
tour.description: The repo also hosts the agent-team harness: guides for the roles, model routing and skill routing, plus Python scripts that lint them. lint_harness.py walks Markdown with harness_markdown.py and checks the contracts declared in harness_routing.py.
tour.languageLesson: Python unittest suites here check docs as data: contract tables in scripts are compared to Markdown so documentation drift fails the tests.
